judged_text: In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares every cal.externalId against a falsy value and can never match, always returning undefined. Reschedules/updates of bookings whose stored reference has no externalCalendarId (exactly the legacy-reference case the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback served) now pass calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, so the update targets the wrong calendar or fails, instead of updating the event on the booking's destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback is now:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
Because the `.find(...)` branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it compares `cal.externalId` against a falsy value (e.g., `undefined/null`) and will not match any normal calendar externalId string. This removes the previous behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) that allowed updates when the stored reference lacked `externalCalendarId` (legacy case), causing `selectedCalendar` to become `undefined` and the update to fall back incorrectly (or fail) instead of targeting the booking’s destination calendar.
